close_reason: Review loop converged: all P1/P2 findings resolved; only P3 opinion items remain
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — Two P0 RFC correctness violations (size field accepted from client; mailboxIds false entries stored) plus one P1 protocol bug (role-uniqueness not guaranteed under backend failure). The rest of the codebase is well-structured and thoughtfully commented. The bugs are all in edge cases or missing validation, not in the core dispatch logic.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — The codebase uses idiomatic Rust for most patterns. Main idiom gaps: BackendChangesError/BackendSetError lack std::error::Error impls (forces verbose map_err on backend implementors); process_update uses Value as its error type instead of a typed enum; role_to_wire silent failure via unwrap_or_default. No unsafe, no gratuitous clones, no ? vs match anti-patterns.
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: the role-vacate race (JMAP-wdy.3) requires a specific failure mode that may not occur with MemoryBackend; there may be additional RFC 8621 field validation gaps I didn't catch without reading the full RFC side-by-side. Uncertainty driven by: not reading RFC 8621 normatively (relied on code comments and field names). Would raise confidence if: ran a conformance test suite like JMAP Tester against MemoryBackend.
Rust idiom confidence: 85% chance of missed issue. Least confident: whether BackendChangesError needs From<E> — might be intentional to force explicit mapping. Uncertainty: didn't check all JMAP-mail-types for missing derives.
title: Review: jmap-mail-server (fresh eyes)
